Extract fitted values from a fast AME fit

Source: R/ame_als.R
fitted.ame_als.Rd

Returns response-scale fitted values: a single matrix for a cross-sectional (ame_als) fit, or a list of matrices for a longitudinal (lame_als) fit.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'ame_als'
fitted(object, plug_in = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

an ame_als object.

plug_in

logical; for an empirical-Bayes binary or count fit, return the plug-in fitted values (TRUE) or the predictive means that integrate the link over the uncertainty of the predictor (FALSE). The default is TRUE for a Poisson fit and FALSE for a binary fit.

...

ignored.

Value

A matrix or list of matrices of fitted values.

Details

For a binary fit the fitted values are predictive probabilities: the expectation of the response over the posterior of the linear predictor, \(\Phi(m / \sqrt{1 + v})\) for a probit link, with \(m\) the posterior mean and \(v\) the posterior variance of the predictor (see predict.ame_als). For a Poisson fit they are the plug-in mean counts, \(e^{\eta + v_e / 2}\) at the fitted predictor \(\eta\) (the posterior mean) and the variance \(v_e\) of the noise of the count, as the samplers report them and as the dynamic empirical-Bayes fit does: the posterior predictive mean of a count is not finite in this model (the inverse-gamma tail of \(v_e\), and the inverse-Wishart tail of the scale of the factors for a cell the data do not inform), so its value would be a property of the numerical integration and of the prior; the plug-in mean is finite everywhere. plug_in = FALSE returns the predictive mean of a count that the integration over the predictor gives, \(e^{m + (v + v_e) / 2}\), and plug_in = TRUE the plug-in values of a binary fit (the response mean at the fitted predictor); the plug-in values are what fit$fitted and fit$YPM hold and simulate() uses. residuals() follows fitted(). The mean of a normal response is its predictor, so a normal fit's fitted values are the posterior means of the predictor, with or without plug_in.

A dynamic fit (lame(method = "als") with dynamic_ab, dynamic_beta or dynamic_uv) follows the same rules. The empirical-Bayes binary fit returns the predictive probability, with \(v\) the variance of the cell's predictor: the additive effects given the coefficients (the prior variance for an actor with no observed cell), the product of the positions, and the coefficients' part at the design asked for; plug_in = TRUE returns \(\Phi(m)\), which fit$fitted keeps. A fit stored without the variance record is an error of class "lame_predictive_missing". The empirical-Bayes count fit returns the plug-in mean \(e^{\eta + v_e / 2}\) and the normal fit the predictor. The dynamic route has no exposure and no forecasts (predict(h > 0) is an error).
